source_description.observation: The space is fairly generous even after the maqaf, yet there is no pointing for אִ֖ישׁ. There is insufficient room for the letters of איש, but ample room for its below-marks (ḥiriq and tipeḥa). MAM's characterization of the space as “narrow” is slightly puzzling. Perhaps “narrow” refers to the room needed for the letters rather than the room needed for the points alone.

parts: יש רווח צר בלבד ואין ניקוד לתיבה "אִ֖ישׁ" הנקראת ולא נכתבת.

translation.text: There is only a narrow space, and no pointing for אִ֖ישׁ, which is read but not written.

comparison.text: MAM calls the space "only a narrow space", although the space appears fairly generous even after the maqaf. The space is insufficient for the qere letters but ample for its below-marks. MAM may mean narrow relative to the room needed for the letters rather than for the points alone. Both the manuscript description and MAM's note say that pointing is absent.

source_description.observation: The tsere and merkha of כֵּ֥ן are written below, between the surrounding written atoms, without the qere letters or dagesh. There is no space above these marks. This reading agrees with MAM’s note.

parts: א=אין רווח לתיבת "כֵּ֥ן" הנקראת ולא נכתבת, אבל נכתבו הצֵרי והמרכא (ולא הדגש, כצפוי) בין התיבות למטה.

translation.text: In the Aleppo Codex, there is no space for כֵּ֥ן, which is read but not written, but the tsere and merkha are written below, between the surrounding written atoms (not the dagesh, as expected).

comparison.text: Both descriptions have tsere and merkha below, no qere letters or dagesh, and no space above the marks.

documentation_notes: The damage to the marginal qere note looks as if opaque tape had been laid parallel to the right margin, obscuring approximately the first letter of each inferred word on its own line. The cause of the damage is unknown. The tape comparison describes how the damage looks; it does not propose a mechanism.

parts: א=הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים [] יְהֹוָֽה (חסר ניקוד ברווח המיועד ל"קרי ולא כתיב")

translation.text: MAM's displayed text agrees with the Leningrad Codex, the Cairo Codex of the Prophets, and the printed editions.
The Aleppo Codex has the following body text:
Pointing is missing from the space intended for "qere without ketiv".
MAM lists Koren, Breuer, the Simanim Tanakh, and Mechon Mamre.

comparison.text: The manuscript description and MAM's note agree that pointing is absent at the qere site. The manuscript description also records the generous spacing and damaged marginal note. MAM reports surrounding text that has not been assessed here: its Aleppo illustration omits נְאֻם־ and has יְהֹוָֽה. Those additional details do not establish a disagreement with the manuscript description.

In the Aleppo Codex there is a noticeable space containing a masorah circle referring to the marginal note, but the vowel points and cantillation marks for the qere, which is read but not written, are missing.
The marginal note says to read אלי.

comparison.text: MAM’s "noticeable space" is compatible with the generous horizontal space described here. The manuscript description and MAM's note agree that pointing is absent. MAM also quotes the marginal note.

translation.text: MAM's qere agrees with the Leningrad Codex's qere.

In the Aleppo Codex there is a noticeable space containing a masorah circle referring to the marginal note, but the vowel points and cantillation marks for the qere, which is read but not written, are missing.

comparison.text: MAM’s "noticeable space" is compatible with the generous end-of-line space described here. The manuscript description and MAM's note agree that pointing is absent. The line ending may explain the generous space accidentally; this is a hypothesis. MAM does not assess whether the space was intentional and also quotes the marginal note.
